name: SparkFun Qwiic Single Relay
description: I2C-controlled relay board: an ATtiny85 running SparkFun's Qwiic Relay firmware drives an Omron G5LE-1 3 VDC SPDT relay (5.5 A continuous at 240 VAC, NO/COM/NC screw terminal) through a transistor. Runs on 3.3 V only, about 100 mA with the relay on; I2C address 0x18 (0x19 with the ADDR jumper closed, or any address set in software). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Single Relay (COM-15093), 2 Qwiic connectors plus a 4-pin 0.1" header GND, 3.3V, SDA, SCL and a 3-way NO/COM/NC screw terminal.
eli5: A switch for big things (lamps, pumps, fans) that your board flips on and off over two I2C wires.

pins.name: 3.3V
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V only (board has no regulator; the 3 V relay coil and ATtiny85 run straight from it). About 100 mA when the relay is on. Never 5 V.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 k pull-up to 3.3 V on the board, jumper JP7)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 k pull-up to 3.3 V on the board, jumper JP7)

buildNotes: Commands are single bytes written to 0x18: 0x01 = relay on, 0x00 = relay off. Write 0x05 then read 1 byte for the state (1 on, 0 off); write 0x04 then read 2 bytes for the firmware version (major, minor).
There is no toggle command: read the state, then send on or off.
Power it from 3.3 V only. The relay coil (23.5 ohm, 3 VDC) sits behind a 10 ohm resistor and pulls about 100 mA, so several boards on one bus may need their own 3.3 V supply.
Closing the ADDR jumper selects 0x19; write 0x03 <addr> to store a new address (0x08-0x77) in EEPROM.
Mains on NO/COM/NC is dangerous: COM to the live wire, NO (off at rest) or NC (on at rest) to the load. Keep fingers off the screw terminal while it is plugged in.
The board has 2.2 k I2C pull-ups; cut JP7 if many pulled-up boards share the bus.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_relay import QwiicRelay

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
relay = QwiicRelay(i2c)  # 0x18; 0x19 with the ADDR jumper closed
print('FW %s' % relay.version())
while True:
    relay.on()
    print('RELAY=%d' % relay.state())
    time.sleep(1)
    relay.off()
    print('RELAY=%d' % relay.state())
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: The relay switches on and off over I2C and reports its state
